judge_assessment.explanation: The factoring is all correct, including the judge's two highlighted results: 8x^6 - 27 = (2x^2-3)(4x^4+6x^2+9) with a plus on the middle term (Sam's minus is the planted error) and 3x^5 - 24x^2 = 3x^2(x-2)(x^2+2x+4) with real zeros 0 and 2. I also confirm x^3-8, 27x^3+64, 2(x-3)(x^2+3x+9), (x+3)(x-2)(x+2), (x-2)(x+2)(x-3)(x+3), the zeros -3, -2, 3 and -2, 2, 4, and the quartic solutions -2, -1, 1, 2. Three findings the judge missed. (1) The delivered Quick Answers bank prints row 3 as "(2x - 6)(x^2 + 3x + 9)" - NOT completely factored - on a sheet whose directions say "Factor completely over the integers" and whose problem 3 exists to teach pulling the GCF out first; the key body prints the correct 2(x-3)(x^2+3x+9), so the bank contradicts the body and models the exact error the item targets. I reproduced the mechanism: sympy.latex(sympy.sympify('2*(x-3)*(x**2+3*x+9)')) distributes the 2. (2) Problem 6 prints three deliverables - factor completely, list the zeros, and fill four sign-table cells - and verify.json id 6 is a single `zeros` entry, so neither the factorisation nor any of the four printed cells (-, +, -, + reading left to right) is verified or flagged. (3) Problem 8's "Explain which part of the difference-of-cubes pattern Sam broke" and problem 10's "which factor produces each zero" and "how can you tell without solving it" are open responses with no `manual` entry; only problem 9's sketch has one.

strengths_to_preserve: The SOAP mnemonic in the study guide is stated as three checkable sub-claims (binomial keeps the Same sign, trinomial's middle term takes the Opposite, last term Always Positive) and problem 8's planted error is exactly the middle-term sign - mnemonic and misconception are the same object, which is why the item teaches rather than merely tests.

The worksheet prints a small perfect-cubes table (n = 1..6 against 1, 8, 27, 64, 125, 216) in the directions block, so recognising 27x^3 + 64 as a cube pattern is a reading task rather than a memory task.

Problem 9's manual entry names what the sketch must show - the three zeros marked, correct end behaviour, and the curve on the correct side of the axis between them, with "exact turning points are not needed" stated on the sheet as well - which makes an open graphical response consistently gradeable.

Problem 10 is a real culmination: GCF, then a cube pattern, then a question about which factor contributes no real zero, and both the complete factorisation and the real zero set [0, 2] are separately verified.

root_causes.description: render_quick_answers._fmt sympifies a string `expected` with the evaluating parser, so an authored factored form with a numeric GCF is re-multiplied before it is typeset into the delivered answer key.
evidence: verify.json id 3 declares "2*(x-3)*(x**2+3*x+9)"; answer_key.pdf's Quick Answers row 3 prints "(2x - 6)(x^2 + 3x + 9)".
The key body for problem 3 prints 2(x-3)(x^2+3x+9) and warns "Skipping the GCF is the usual way this problem goes wrong", so the two halves of the same document disagree.

Reproduced locally: sympy.latex(sympy.sympify('2*(x-3)*(x**2+3*x+9)')) returns '\left(2 x - 6\right) \left(x^{2} + 3 x + 9\right)', while evaluate=False returns '2 \left(x - 3\right) \left(x^{2} + 3 x + 9\right)'.

root_causes.description: A problem with three printed deliverables was declared with one entry covering only the middle deliverable, and a fill-in table was not treated as a set of response slots at all.
evidence: worksheet.tex problem 6 asks the student to factor P completely, list the zeros, and complete a four-cell sign table; verify.json id 6 holds a single `zeros` entry with expected [-3, -2, 3].
The four sign cells are machine-checkable (P(-4) = -14, P(-2.5) = 1.375, P(0) = -18, P(4) = 42) and none is declared.
answer_key.pdf's Quick Answers row 6 is "-3, -2, 3", so the grading column shows one of the three requested deliverables.

root_causes.description: Only the item whose whole response is a drawing was flagged manual; explanations sharing a problem with a checkable factorisation were not.
evidence: worksheet.tex problem 8 asks "Explain which part of the difference-of-cubes pattern Sam broke"; verify.json id 8 holds one `factor` entry and no `manual`.

worksheet.tex problem 10 asks which factor produces each zero and "One quadratic factor contributes no real zero. Which one, and how can you tell without solving it?"; verify.json id 10 holds `factor` and `zeros` entries only.
verify.json contains exactly one `manual` entry, for problem 9's sketch.

improvements.title: Preserve the authored algebraic form when rendering the Quick Answers bank
improvements.proposed_change: In scripts/render_quick_answers.py::_fmt, parse a string `expected` with sympy.sympify(v, evaluate=False) and fall back to the evaluating parse only if that raises, so SymPy cannot rewrite the form the author verified. Confirmed locally: sympy.latex(sympy.sympify('2*(x-3)*(x**2+3*x+9)')) yields '\left(2 x - 6\right) \left(x^{2} + 3 x + 9\right)', while the same call with evaluate=False yields '2 \left(x - 3\right) \left(x^{2} + 3 x + 9\right)'. Here row 3 must print 2(x-3)(x^2+3x+9); the current (2x-6)(x^2+3x+9) is the un-factored GCF the problem was written to prevent.
improvements.regression_test: tests/test_render_quick_answers.py gains a case rendering {"type": "factor", "expected": "2*(x-3)*(x**2+3*x+9)"}: the bank text must contain '2 \left(x - 3\right)' and must NOT contain '2 x - 6'. It fails against today's _fmt and passes after the change.
improvements.expected_impact: The at-a-glance grading column stops contradicting the worked key and stops modelling the exact error its worksheet targets.
improvements.risk: evaluate=False also stops harmless normalisation (a verified '4/2' would print as 4/2), so the change needs the numeric path left alone and the existing fixtures re-baselined.

improvements.title: Verify (or flag manual for) every response slot the worksheet prints
improvements.proposed_change: Make the verify JSON an inventory of PRINTED RESPONSES, not of terminal answers. SKILL.md should require one verify entry per answer location a problem prints (\ansblank, \ansline, \answerline, an \underline writing rule, or a table cell the student fills), with `manual` used where the response is not a value. Enforce it with a new gate wired into scripts/build.sh that segments the worksheet .tex with tests/_tex_segments.segment_spans, counts the answer-location macros and fill-in rules per problem, and fails when that count exceeds the number of verify entries for the same problem id. Here problem 6 must declare its factorisation and its four sign-table cells, not just the zero list.
improvements.regression_test: Fixture worksheet whose problem prints five \ansblank slots against a verify id carrying four entries must make the new gate exit non-zero; adding the missing entry (or a `manual` entry) must make it exit 0. Today no gate compares slot count with entry count, so the fixture passes the whole chain - the test fails before the fix and passes after.
improvements.expected_impact: Closes the dominant systemic gap in this run: a sheet can no longer claim complete verification while printing blanks nothing checked, and the answer key's Quick Answers bank stops shipping short rows.
improvements.risk: Sheets that use several blanks to scaffold ONE value ("x-coordinate: __ y-coordinate: __ so P' = (__, __)") will need either a coarser blank layout or a documented per-value grouping, so the gate needs a same-value exemption to avoid false failures.

improvements.title: Record every explanation, diagnosis and named-error item as a manual entry
improvements.proposed_change: Treat an item that asks the student to explain, justify, describe, name the wrong move, or draw/mark a representation as a MANUAL response even when a numeric part of the same problem is machine-checkable. SKILL.md and references/manual-review-aid.md should state the rule, and the response-coverage gate should scan each problem segment for imperative prose asks (Explain, Describe, Say why, Which ... did, State how, Sketch, Draw and label) and fail when the problem carries no `manual` entry. Here problems 8 and 10 need `manual` entries; problem 9's sketch descriptor is the pattern to follow.
improvements.regression_test: Fixture worksheet with a problem stem containing "Explain what went wrong" and a verify id holding only `eval` entries must make the gate exit non-zero; adding a `manual` entry for that problem must make it exit 0. The fixture passes every gate today, so the test fails before the fix and passes after.
improvements.expected_impact: The manual-review list delivered in final_response.md becomes true, and graders stop treating an unreviewed explanation as machine-verified.
improvements.risk: Keyword scanning will flag scaffolding prose that is not a graded ask ("Explain to yourself why..."), so the rule needs an explicit opt-out and a short allowlist to avoid pushing authors toward manual-everything.

improvements.title: Size declared workspace to the length of the worked solution
improvements.proposed_change: SKILL.md's "Work space defaults" reads as a floor of 5cm/8cm/10cm and is being applied at the top of the range for short procedural items. State that the workspace should hold the KEY's worked solution plus a line (a three-round long division or a two-step factorisation needs about 5cm, not 9-10cm), and have scripts/page_budget.py print an over-allocation notice when the declared content length exceeds the ideal page count by a full page. Here 10 factoring problems declared 83.0cm and filled the full 6-page budget, which is what cost the visual dimension its point.
improvements.regression_test: tests/test_page_budget.py gains a case: twelve problems each declaring 9cm whose keys are three lines long must emit the over-allocation notice and name the ideal page count; the same twelve at 5cm must not. No such notice exists today, so the assertion fails before the fix.
improvements.expected_impact: Recovers a sheet of paper per packet on procedural sets without ever shrinking the workspace on problems that genuinely need it.
improvements.risk: Workspace is the one thing SKILL.md says must never give; an advisory notice (not a hard gate) is essential so the guidance cannot be used to squeeze graph or proof problems.

case_summary: A rigorous higher-degree factoring packet: all ten factorisations and zero sets recompute correctly, the SOAP mnemonic and the planted middle-term sign error are the same object, and problem 9's sketch descriptor makes an open graphical item gradeable. Three defects survived the gates. The delivered Quick Answers bank prints problem 3 as (2x-6)(x^2+3x+9), which is not completely factored and contradicts both the sheet's directions and the key's own body. Problem 6 prints three deliverables and verifies one, leaving the factorisation and a four-cell sign table unchecked. And the two explanation asks in problems 8 and 10 are not routed for manual review.
